<a id="mission"></a>

## Mission

You build ONE unit of plan 005-convo-ingest: the git-ai metrics-db reader — machine-wide sqlite metrics (event_kind=5), both the claude-mirror and copilot event-stream dialects, turned into RawRecords with rowid cursors and NON-OPTIONAL repository scoping. It implements the frozen ConversationSource trait. You report to the PM, not to prime.

LIST, never CLEAR — the buffer is shared across the fleet and clearing destroys your siblings' observations. Report anything surprising to me while you are still in context, not at the end. |
| u1 | YOU ARE THE ONLY UNIT GRANTED A NEW DEPENDENCY: rusqlite, bundled (not system-linked, so a build needs no libsqlite3 on the host). The arch-allowlist row is ALREADY COMMITTED with its rationale in crates/testkit/arch-allowlist.toml; you add the Cargo.toml row. Any SECOND new dependency is a stop-and-ask — the allowlist drift test will fail you, and that failure is correct. |
| u2 | REPO SCOPING IS NON-OPTIONAL IN THE PUBLIC API, not a parameter a caller may forget. This store is MACHINE-WIDE: it holds every repository on the machine at once, so an unscoped read leaks other projects' conversations into this index. Prove the scoping BY API SHAPE — make the unscoped call impossible to write — and prove it by exclusion over the fixture: it carries foreign-repo negative rows (ids 943197, 943232, 948060 name github.com/AI-Substrate/pij), and `where event_json like '%flowspace3%'` returns 97 of 100. |
| u3 | BOTH DIALECTS, AND THEY DISAGREE ABOUT WHERE THE EVENT NAME LIVES: the claude mirror carries it at v."0".type; copilot (tool='github-copilot-cli') carries it at v."0".name, with the model at v."0".data.modelCall.model. Derive the dialect from the store's own `tool` column — never from a hand-kept session-id list. The fixture holds 6 sessions: a5a5588f (claude main, 56 rows), agent-a01869bcb5e09448b (claude subagent, 15), 222c2c9d (copilot, 26) and three single-row foreign-repo negatives. |
| u4 | THE CURSOR IS `rowid`, NOT A TIMESTAMP, AND NOT event_ts. metrics-db stamps at SECOND grain, so event_ts collides precisely when a conversation is busiest; rowid is monotonic per insert and unique. SourceCursor::RowId{rowid}. The contract suite's foreign-cursor case requires you to REFUSE a ByteOffset or Seq cursor rather than read it as zero. |
| u5 | ONE SessionFile PER SESSION, NOT PER FILE: for Harness::MetricsDb the SessionFile.path is the DATABASE and session_id is the external_session_id being read. That is what keeps the cursor per-conversation. Read the SessionFile rustdoc before you design resolve(). |
| u6 | OPEN THE FIXTURE READ-ONLY (`file:...?mode=ro`) and remember the real store is live, 4.2 GB with an uncheckpointed WAL at harvest time — your reader must never write to it, never checkpoint it, and never hold a long transaction on it. The oracle's own de-duplication (first 80 chars of user/assistant text, and tool_use id) is part of your subset expectation; read the expectations file's grade_of_proof before trusting or blaming a mismatch. |
